title: gentiana crassuloides subsp. curviphylla
intro: Gentiana crassuloides subsp. curviphylla, commonly known as Tibetan gentian, is a species of flowering plant in the gentian family, native to the Himalayas. It has been traditionally used in Tibetan medicine to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and gastrointestinal issues, due to its potential health benefits such as anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antiviral properties. The therapeutic actions of Tibetan gentian are attributed to its ability to stimulate digestion, reduce inflammation, and enhance immune function, making it a valued plant in traditional medicine. The bioactive constituents of Tibetan gentian include iridoids, gentiopicroside, loganic acid, and swertiamarin, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
